_comment: Concept self-quiz for the Education hub. answer = index of the correct choice.

questions.q: What triggers Dictyostelium amoebae to begin multicellular development?
questions.explain: Starvation initiates development: cells stop dividing and begin secreting and sensing cAMP to aggregate.

questions.q: Which molecule do cells chemotax toward during aggregation?
questions.explain: Aggregating cells chemotax toward cAMP. (Folate guides feeding amoebae toward bacteria.)

questions.q: In the migrating slug, where are the future spore (prespore) cells located?
questions.explain: Prestalk cells occupy the anterior ~20%; prespore cells make up the posterior region.

questions.q: The Dictyostelium stalk is made of cells that…
questions.explain: Stalk cells vacuolate and die to hold the spore mass aloft — a classic example of altruistic cell death.

questions.q: Which morphogen promotes prestalk/stalk cell fate?
questions.explain: DIF-1 (Differentiation-Inducing Factor 1), a chlorinated polyketide, induces prestalk/stalk differentiation.

questions.q: Roughly how long does development take, from starvation to fruiting body?
questions.explain: Under standard conditions the whole program — aggregation through culmination — takes about 24 hours.

questions.q: Why is Dictyostelium a useful model for human disease?
choices: Many of its genes have human orthologs (e.g. CLN5)
questions.explain: Despite being an amoeba, it shares many disease-relevant genes with humans — e.g. CLN5 (Batten disease).

questions.q: What does a vegetative (feeding) amoeba eat, and how?
questions.explain: Feeding amoebae engulf bacteria by phagocytosis — the basis for using Dictyostelium to study phagocytes.

questions.q: Which structure disperses to start the next generation?
questions.explain: Spores in the sorus are dispersed and germinate into new amoebae when conditions improve.

questions.q: What guides the migrating slug toward the soil surface?
questions.explain: The slug migrates toward light and warmth (photo- and thermotaxis), bringing it to the surface for spore dispersal.
